subject.title: [Architecture] Extract terminal execution drivers from agent-core packages

question: Should OpenClaw retain the current generic agent-core callback boundary, or introduce a new shared terminal-driver contract across the built-in Pi and Codex runtime paths?
rationale: The request changes a core ownership and security boundary, while its proposed paths do not identify the actual driver code, consumers, dependency savings, or relationship to the active RuntimePlan cleanup plan.

options.title: Retain current ownership
options.body: Keep terminal execution implementation with each runtime owner and limit agent-core to generic contracts unless concrete duplicated mechanics are demonstrated.

options.title: Sponsor a terminal-driver package
options.body: Define a leaf-safe package contract, dependency graph, consumer migration, and explicit exclusions for approvals, sandboxing, and runtime-specific process policy before implementation.

options.title: Fold into RuntimePlan RFC
options.body: Expand https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/72072 to own this extraction after confirming it fits that roadmap’s runner decomposition.

recommendation.title: Retain current ownership
recommendation.body: Keep terminal execution implementation with each runtime owner and limit agent-core to generic contracts unless concrete duplicated mechanics are demonstrated.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged RuntimePlan/Harness work and active finalization RFC are the closest established architecture ownership signals.
